lines.text: It's 2014, at an airport in China. Dawn Michelle Hunt, an American from Chicago, is checking two bags for the next flight of a trip she won.
lines.style: a documentary narrator telling a true story: low, controlled, quiet intensity, close to the microphone, never theatrical; present tense, close, quick

lines.text: Not long after, security staff call her aside. She is led into a room, and her two bags are already there.
lines.style: a documentary narrator telling a true story: low, controlled, quiet intensity, close to the microphone, never theatrical; present tense, close, quick

lines.text: The officers want to know one thing. Are these bags hers?
lines.style: a documentary narrator telling a true story: low, controlled, quiet intensity, close to the microphone, never theatrical; present tense, close, quick

lines.text: According to her brother, she says yes.
lines.style: a documentary narrator telling a true story: low, controlled, quiet intensity, close to the microphone, never theatrical; present tense, close, quick

lines.text: Why would she say anything else? She packed them herself. She just paid to carry them.
lines.style: a documentary narrator telling a true story: low, controlled, quiet intensity, close to the microphone, never theatrical; present tense, close, quick

lines.text: Inside the luggage are designer handbags. And sewn into the linings of those handbags, authorities say, is more than two kilograms of methamphetamine.
lines.style: a documentary narrator telling a true story: low, controlled, quiet intensity, close to the microphone, never theatrical; present tense, close, quick

lines.text: Her family says she had no idea it was there. She believed the handbags were a prize, from the people who had paid for the trip of her life.
lines.style: a documentary narrator telling a true story: low, controlled, quiet intensity, close to the microphone, never theatrical; present tense, close, quick

lines.text: The luggage was hers. The drugs, she said, were not.
lines.style: a documentary narrator telling a true story: low, controlled, quiet intensity, close to the microphone, never theatrical; present tense, close, quick

lines.text: Three years later, a court sentences her to death, with a two-year reprieve. Today, she is serving life.
lines.style: a documentary narrator telling a true story: low, controlled, quiet intensity, close to the microphone, never theatrical; present tense, close, quick

lines.text: And twelve years after that airport, her brother appears before American lawmakers with a question that no one in the room can answer.
